options: The producer waits for the leader broker AND enough in-sync replicas to acknowledge the write before considering it done
The producer never waits for any acknowledgment
The producer waits only for the consumer to read the message
The producer sends the same event to every topic in the cluster
questions.explain: acks=all is the strongest durability setting — a write isn't acknowledged until it's durable across brokers, not just the leader.

questions.q: Why isn't `acks=all` simply the right answer for every producer?
options: It's slower than acks=0 or acks=1, so high-volume, loss-tolerant telemetry may reasonably choose a faster setting instead
acks=all is actually not supported by any real Kafka client
acks=all makes a producer send events to the wrong partition
acks=all disables all partitioning entirely
questions.explain: It's a genuine trade-off: acks=0 fits high-volume, loss-tolerant data; acks=all fits data where losing an event has a real cost.

questions.q: What happens if a producer sends events for the same order_id with no key at all, when ordering for that order matters?
options: Round-robin partitioning may scatter those events across different partitions, silently breaking their relative ordering
Kafka automatically detects the missing key and assigns one for you
The produce call is rejected until a key is supplied
Nothing changes — ordering is guaranteed across the whole topic regardless of key
questions.explain: Without a key, there's no guarantee those events land in the same partition, which is what per-entity ordering depends on.

options: How long a producer waits to batch more events together before sending, trading a little latency for higher throughput
How long a consumer waits between poll() calls
How long a broker retains a partition's data before deleting it
How many replicas a partition must have
questions.explain: linger.ms lets a producer accumulate a batch instead of sending every event as a separate tiny request, improving overall throughput.

questions.q: What does `batch.size` do in combination with `linger.ms`?
options: It sets the max bytes a producer accumulates before sending a batch, regardless of whether linger.ms's wait window has elapsed
It sets the number of partitions a topic can have
It sets how many consumers can join a consumer group
It has no relationship to linger.ms at all
questions.explain: batch.size forces a send once enough bytes have accumulated, even if the linger.ms timer hasn't yet expired.
